items.comment:
🔴 **Critical** `reducers/license_management.ts:74`

The `?? 0` fallback causes licenses without an expiration date to always return `true` from `isExpired`. When `getExpirationMillis(state)` returns `undefined` (e.g., for basic licenses), the expression `new Date().getTime() > 0` is always true. This incorrectly marks basic and unlicensed states as expired, propagating through `shouldShowRevertToBasicLicense`, `shouldShowStartTrial`, and `getLicenseState` to show incorrect UI elements.

items.comment:
🟠 **High** `actions/clear_cache_indices.ts:24`

The type assertion `(error as { body: { message: string } }).body.message` crashes at runtime when the error lacks a `body` property. Network errors, timeouts, and other non-HTTP exceptions don't have the expected shape, causing `TypeError: Cannot read property 'message' of undefined`. The pattern in `reload_indices.ts` uses safe optional chaining (`httpError.body?.message ?? ''`) to handle this.
<details>
<summary>Also found in 3 other location(s)</summary>

`x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/index_management/public/application/store/actions/forcemerge_indices.ts:24`

> Unsafe type assertion on error object will crash if error doesn't have `body.message` structure. If the caught error is a network error, JavaScript Error, or any object without a `body` property, accessing `(error as { body: { message: string } }).body.message` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'message' of undefined`. The similar `reloadIndices` function in the same codebase uses safer optional chaining: `httpError.body?.message ?? ''`.

`x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/index_management/public/application/store/actions/close_indices.ts:23`

> Unsafe type assertion on `error` can cause a runtime crash if the error doesn't have a `body` property. Network errors, timeouts, or other non-HTTP exceptions won't have the expected `{ body: { message: string } }` structure. Accessing `(error as { body: { message: string } }).body.message` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'message' of undefined` when `body` is undefined. Compare with `reload_indices.ts` which uses defensive access: `httpError.body?.message ?? ''`.

`x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/index_management/public/application/store/actions/open_indices.ts:24`

> Unsafe type assertion on `error` can cause a runtime crash if the error doesn't have a `body` property. Network errors, timeouts, or other non-HTTP exceptions won't have the expected `{ body: { message: string } }` structure. Accessing `(error as { body: { message: string } }).body.message` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'message' of undefined` when `body` is undefined. Compare with `reload_indices.ts` which uses defensive access: `httpError.body?.message ?? ''`.

</details>

items.comment:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Unsafe error cast may throw in the catch block itself.**

If `error` lacks the `{ body: { message: string } }` shape (network failure, unexpected exception type), accessing `.body.message` throws an uncaught error, losing both error handling and original context.

This pattern repeats in `refresh_indices.ts`, `forcemerge_indices.ts`, and `extension_action.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Suggested safer approach</summary>

```diff
-    } catch (error: unknown) {
-      notificationService.showDangerToast((error as { body: { message: string } }).body.message);
+    } catch (error: unknown) {
+      const message =
+        typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'body' in error
+          ? (error as { body?: { message?: string } }).body?.message
+          : undefined;
+      notificationService.showDangerToast(message ?? 'An unexpected error occurred');
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In
`@x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/index_management/public/application/store/actions/close_indices.ts`
around lines 22 - 24, The catch blocks currently unsafely cast error to { body:
{ message: string } } and access .body.message which can throw; update the error
handling in close_indices.ts (the catch in the async action that calls
notificationService.showDangerToast and dispatch(clearRowStatus({ indexNames
}))) to safely derive a message using optional chaining and fallbacks (e.g.,
check error && (error as any).body?.message or use String(error) /
error.message) before calling notificationService.showDangerToast, ensuring
dispatch(clearRowStatus({ indexNames })) still runs; apply the same
safe-extraction pattern to the analogous catch blocks in refresh_indices.ts,
forcemerge_indices.ts, and extension_action.ts so no catch throws while
formatting the error message.
```

</details>

Non-blocking. Some comments on the diag logging here:

- Eventually there will be an SDK metric to monitor this (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/otel/sdk-metrics/#metric-otelsdkprocessorlogprocessed), which will be nice.
- The `_droppedLogRecordsCount` var name is a little misleading. I did a double-take when I saw it being reset to 0 after logging about a few being dropped. Maybe `_numDroppedSinceLastWarn` or something.

E.g. with [a play app](https://gist.github.com/trentm/0b1ef3b551b543c67ba33a922efab4a9) that is hitting the limit, I get the following logging.  Every `.` is a one-second heartbeat. items.comment:
Attempting to fully flush the *live* `_finishedLogRecords` can **fail to complete**, if the app is adding records faster than the export can handle. The spec says (emphasis mine):

> any tasks associated with LogRecords **for which the LogRecordProcessor had already received events prior to the call to ForceFlush** SHOULD be completed as soon as possible

So we can grab the current set of `_finishedLogRecords` when `_flushAll` is called and process only those.

I have a starter patch to handle this and the issue above, for discussion:
https://gist.github.com/trentm/76059c60c43257f04e44038b0471d970#file-the-diff
